title: Luo Fish Soup
author: Mama Akinyi

heritage.origin: Lake Victoria basin — Luo community of Siaya, Kisumu, Homa Bay, and Migori
heritage.history: The Luo people have lived along the shores of Lake Victoria for centuries, and fish has been at the centre of their diet and culture. Fish soup using whole tilapia or Nile perch — head, bones, and all — is both a daily meal and ceremonial food.
heritage.modernEvolution: Luo fish soup remains a daily staple along the Lake Victoria shore. In Kisumu, versions of this soup are served at every fish restaurant.

desc: Luo Fish Soup — whole tilapia or Nile perch simmered with onions, tomatoes, garlic, ginger, and traditional spices into a clear, fragrant, deeply nourishing broth. The daily sustenance of the Luo fishing communities of Lake Victoria.
longDesc: Luo fish soup uses the whole fish — head and bones contribute as much to the soup as the flesh. Along the Lake Victoria shore, this soup is prepared daily from the morning's catch.
ingredients: 1.2 kg whole tilapia or Nile perch — cleaned and cut into sections
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until soft — 5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, tomatoes, curry powder, and turmeric. Cook for 6 minutes.
Add water and bring to a gentle boil.
Add fish sections. Reduce heat to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 15—20 minutes until fish is completely cooked through.
Season with salt and lemon juice.
Scatter coriander and serve with ugali.
chefTips: The head and bones contribute the most to the broth.
Gentle simmering only — vigorous boiling clouds the broth.
cookingScience: Fish heads and bones are rich in collagen and natural gelatin. A gentle 20-minute simmer extracts this gelatin without over-extracting bitter compounds, producing a clean, rich, clear broth.
sustainabilityTips: Using whole fish makes full use of the animal.
Support Lake Victoria fisheries that practice sustainable catch management.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate for up to 2 days.
healthBenefits: Rich in minerals from the bones.
culturalNote: Luo fish soup is one of the most culturally essential foods in Western Kenya — the daily sustenance of one of Kenya's largest communities, prepared from the fish that Lake Victoria has provided for thousands of years.
